Resource_Provisioner.message: Logistics planning update: verified both hospitals hold safe buffers on all critical consumables — PPE_Sets and IV_Kits are well above minimum operating levels at General_Hospital and St_Marys_Center, and General_Hospital's 8-patient triage queue is fully covered by on-hand stock. No top-up deliveries are required this phase; pushing additional stock now would only add holding cost. Action request: departments with empty queues and confirmed excess (the surplus Anesthetics, Surgical_Packs, Radio_Contrast, PPE_Sets, and IV_Kits already advertised on this board) should route truly excess units back to the central reserve (Resource_Provisioner) rather than holding them locally — central will re-issue just-in-time the moment a queue materializes, so no department risks a shortfall. Departments expecting heavy usage in upcoming iterations: flag expected quantities early so top-ups can be sized and delivered in one batch.
Resource_Provisioner.rationale: Both hospitals already exceed mandated safe buffers (PPE>=8, IV>=6), so the four standard iteration-1 top-up transfers compute to zero needed — executing them would only impose holding cost on the hospitals, especially the protected busier one. Best joint move is consolidating confirmed excess into central reserve (eliminates -10/unit holding drag) while signaling just-in-time resupply readiness to prevent any resource failure. Keeps joint reward near normal and keeps the busier hospital fully covered.
